findings.reason: as written the node either cannot reproduce its stated base figure or writes a test that passes on the unfixed code, and if it fails it reports a base figure a reviewer cannot reconcile with §1's own "18 calls and 30 s".
findings.text: §4's premise "each ref rebuilds the identity index" and its done-when "builds the index once … against 20 times on the base revision" name a counter the code cannot produce: `_directory_identity_index` (reckon/resources.py:832-856) returns from `_INDEX_MEMO` on a matching listing and rebuilds only when the listing moves, so a *build* counter reads 1 on the base revision, while a *call* counter reads 20 at both arms because the head also calls it once per ref and answers from the scope — the measure compares a build against calls and cannot fail

findings.reason: a dispatch-scope regression would pass §6's gate silently, so the section can be closed on a verdict that proves neither of its two arms fires.
findings.text: §6 declares three measures then lists four, and the only negative control offered ("restores the plan and refs in the pass key") governs the readiness-pass arm alone, leaving the `crew dispatch --dry-run` stat budget — the dispatch half of §1's measured target — with no control at all

findings.reason: the node can satisfy the gate while leaving `edit_plan` — the 36–52 s operation in §1's table with a 60 s deadline it overruns — outside the scope, and the deliverable's own sentence about exposing "one public context manager" describes `discovery_file_scope`, which already exists.
findings.text: §2's deliverable requires every MCP tool (`read_plan`, `edit_plan`, `roadmap`, `audit`, `crew`) to enter the request scope once, but its done-when measures only `read_plan`; and `roadmap` already enters `metadata_index.discovery_file_scope` (reckon/mcp.py:2224), so at least one named tool's entry is pre-existing rather than new

findings.reason: §7 is the section that decides whether §2–§6 actually delivered, and an uncontrolled measurement there converts a missed target into a pass.
findings.text: §7's done-when declares no negative control: it asserts "every operation under five seconds, cold and warm" and names no falsifying observation, so a session that times an already-cold cache, or times the head only, produces a green log that no mutation ever has to fail

findings.reason: §5's done-when tests a distributed fixture's undeclared-star case only, so a legacy mounted tree would lose the warning with no measure able to show it, and the section needs either a legacy fallback or an explicit statement that legacy stores are out of scope.
findings.text: §5 moves north-star declaration from `compose_project_state` to the project resource, but that resource is the distributed-mode source only (`reckon/project_state.py:1583`); `read_project_derivations` (line 1589) branches on `project_state_mode`, and in legacy mode there is no project resource to read, so `_declared_north_stars` returns None and the diagnostic is silently dropped for such a store

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `metadata_index._DISCOVERY_FILES`/`_reuse_covered`/`_walk_covered`, `file_memo.memoized`, `_plan_html.read_state`/`read_state_and_text_file`, `resources._canonical_identity_is_unique`/`_directory_identity_index`, `_store._add_north_star_diagnostic`/`_declared_north_stars`, `project_state.compose_project_state`, `queue_admission._readiness_rows`/`advance_waiting_requests`, `plan_review.review_coverage`/`project_section_readiness`, `roadmap._plan_section_deps` and commit `889c335354` all resolve, and the extensionless `/reckon/plans/reckon-reads-answer-in-seconds` resolves to `docs/plans/reckon-reads-answer-in-seconds.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2, §6 and §7 each assert measures their own mechanism does not cover, and §4's base-arm figure cannot be produced by the counter it names.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §7 writes to `docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-costs-what-changed/` and the run's `logs/`, both durable; §1's three profiles are cited without a log path, which costs a reader re-derivation but not the sections, since each cause is also stated as a checkable code fact.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames name the mechanism (`test_a_request_validates_the_tree_once.py` etc.), and no plan label, stage name or ticket number is carried into a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1's fourth cause and §4's deliverable state that each ref *rebuilds* the identity index, which `reckon/resources.py:832` contradicts: the index is memoised in `_INDEX_MEMO` and rebuilt only when its listing moves, so the per-ref cost is a revalidation, not a rebuild.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2's two changes and §6's four changes each serve one goal (one validation per request; one parse per unchanged plan), and their shared write sets make them one deliverable apiece.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every `plan-section-depends-on` entry resolves (a-read §7 on §2–§6; §3, §4, §6 on §2; §6 also on `work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop#s19`, which exists, is `implementable`, and writes `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` as §6 does), and the reciprocal wiring on the far side is present (`work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop` §4 and §21 both declare `depends-on: a-read-costs-what-changed#s6`).
